# Owner direction — Polaris dossiers generated by the operator's own agent session

Date: 2026-10-05

Owner: Tzeusy

Decision ID: `POLARIS-DOSSIER-LOCAL-AGENT-MODE-2026-10-05`

This is a plain owner direction in the shape of
`POLARIS-LANE-B-DECLINED-AND-TARGET-REVISED-DIRECTION.md`. It binds no
artifact digest, adds no row to `ACCEPTANCE-ACT-RECORD.md` and registers
nothing. It authorizes drafting and review. It does not amend the generator
specification, and it does not authorize implementation that depends on an
amendment. Only the owner's sign-off of the reviewed amendment does that
(VIS-4).

## The owner's words

On 2026-10-05, in the Claude Code CLI, the owner was told that a Redis dossier
run would need an Anthropic API key, because the Syzygy process itself would
call the model. The owner wrote:

> Why do you need an anthropic api key? The usage of the LLM to generate the
> dossier should be purely done by a human using claude-code or codex, a
> provided syzygy binary, and the target codebase cloned locally? No api key
> involved

The owner then answered three structured questions. The options selected,
with their descriptions as shown, follow.

**Q1.** "When your Claude Code / Codex session generates the dossier, how much
of the local clone should the agent read on its own?"

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| "Agent explores freely" | "The agent reads the clone with its own tools; syzygy supplies prompts and output schema, then validates and renders. Likely a richer page, but 'what was read' becomes the agent's self-report and the not-read accounting weakens." |

**Q2.** The question asked whether the owner directs this local-agent mode, so
that the amendment can be drafted and the mode built. It quoted the draft
direction:

> Polaris dossiers are generated by the operator's own Claude Code or Codex
> session over a local clone at a consented revision, exploring freely.
> Syzygy supplies the brief, the output schema, quote/label/citation checks
> against the pinned blobs, a fresh-context fidelity review step and the
> renderer. Syzygy makes no provider call. The provider-route and egress
> packages are parked.

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| "Yes, as drafted (Recommended)" | "Recorded as a plain owner direction (no digest). I draft the CC-REV-2 amendment, get it reviewed, bring it to you for a version-tag sign-off, then implement. Spec drafting and the binary's design start now; code that depends on the amendment waits for your sign-off." |

**Q3.** "How should Syzygy treat your agent session sending Redis content to
Anthropic/OpenAI?"

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| "Operator's own act (Recommended)" | "Outside Syzygy's egress consent: Syzygy sends nothing, so no egress record. The dossier page and run record disclose that the agent read the clone unrestricted and that its reading account is self-reported [Inferred]; quotes stay byte-verified." |

## The direction

1. **The mode.** A Polaris dossier is generated by the operator's own Claude
   Code or Codex session over a local clone at a consented revision, and the
   session explores the clone freely. Syzygy supplies the brief, the output
   schema, quote, label and citation checks against the pinned Git blobs, a
   fresh-context fidelity review step, and the renderer. Syzygy makes no
   provider call.
2. **Egress reading (owner ruling).** The operator's agent session sending
   target content to its own provider is the operator's own act. It is outside
   Syzygy's egress consent, and no egress record is required for it. The
   dossier page and its run record must disclose that the agent read the
   clone without restriction and that its account of what it read is
   self-reported (Inferred). Every rendered quotation stays byte-verified
   against the pinned blobs.
3. **What still binds Syzygy's own reads.** Syzygy still reads the clone's
   Git objects at the pinned commit, to verify quotations and render source
   pages. Those reads still need the target's observation consent, the
   observer registry entry, and the classification and screening policy acts,
   unchanged. This direction relaxes none of them.
4. **Parked.** The provider-route registry entries, the egress v1 and v2
   packages and the provider adapter are parked: not offered for sign-off,
   not deleted. Work they share with this mode, such as the consent reader
   and revision pinning, continues.
5. **Amendment path.** The adopted generator specification is written for
   Syzygy-made provider calls: stage budgets, provider receipts, the
   registered route, and the independence of the fidelity review. The
   affected requirements are amended through one reviewed CC-REV-2 delta,
   which binds only on the owner's sign-off. Implementation that depends on
   it waits for that sign-off.

## What this direction does not do

- It does not amend doctrine. SEC-2 is read, not changed: the ruling in item 2
  concerns who sends, not whether consent is needed for Syzygy's own sends.
- It does not adopt, accept or sign any package, and it labels nothing
  accepted.
- It does not withdraw any act in force.
